query: What features can be extracted from a company's business description to predict its regional cluster?

per_column.name: dominant_industry
per_column.rationale: Industry mix varies geographically (e.g., semiconductor/AI concentrations differ by region), so an industry label derived from the description is a legitimate, non-leaking predictor of regional cluster and plausibly carries real signal.

per_column.name: description_length
per_column.rationale: Bucketed text length is a mechanical, generic feature with no plausible semantic link to geographic region; it does not carry regional signal.

per_column.name: is_b2b
per_column.rationale: Business model (B2B vs. not) is external to region and can co-vary with regional industry ecosystems, giving weak but plausible predictive signal for the cluster.

per_column.name: has_rd_focus
per_column.rationale: R&D orientation tends to concentrate in specific tech/research hubs, so it lies outside the focus and can carry regional signal; however its extreme imbalance (6/199) limits real leverage.

per_column.name: tech_depth_score
per_column.rationale: A measure of technical depth from the description is an external attribute that may correlate with tech-heavy regions; heavy skew toward 0 limits its usefulness but it is a legitimate predictor.

judge.rationale: Four of five columns are legitimate, non-leaking predictors derived from the description, with dominant_industry offering the most genuine geographic signal. However, is_b2b, has_rd_focus, and tech_depth_score are all heavily imbalanced (near-constant), sharply reducing their discriminative power, and description_length is a mechanical filler with no regional relevance. Notably, the original table already contains City/Latitude/Longitude, which likely define the cluster far more directly; the added text-derived features add only modest incremental leverage as a set.
